What the ruling does not yet tell us: whether the reasoning holds on rehearing or at the Supreme Court, and whether other states will structure new detention facilities to follow the template. Judge Nancy Abudu's dissent argues the majority minimized federal involvement.

Florida was promised federal reimbursement. DeSantis announced a FEMA grant of more than $600 million for the facility in October 2025. The court held that because no money had actually changed hands by the injunction, the project remained a state action for NEPA purposes.

The part worth dwelling on is the reasoning itself. It disaggregates who built a facility from who uses it. A state can construct a detention site on its own land, transfer operational control to ICE, and the resulting infrastructure may be insulated from federal review.

Pryor's logic: because Florida constructed the facility with state funds, and had received no federal reimbursement when the injunction was issued, there was no "major federal action" to trigger NEPA. Operational support from ICE after the fact did not change that.

The Everglades facility was built in eight days on the Dade-Collier airstrip, is operated by the Florida Division of Emergency Management, and holds ICE detainees. Friends of the Everglades, the Center for Biological Diversity, and the Miccosukee Tribe brought the suit.

The 2-1 ruling vacates U.S. District Judge Kathleen Williams's August 2025 injunction, which required the facility to wind down for failing federal environmental review. Majority: Chief Judge William Pryor (Bush appointee) and Judge Andrew Brasher (Trump appointee).

On Tuesday, the 11th Circuit ruled that "Alligator Alcatraz" can stay open because Florida (not the federal government) built and controls it. The reasoning matters more than the outcome. It is a blueprint for shielding detention facilities from federal legal challenge.

It’s a little after 3:00 PM which means it’s time to go through my daily ritual of realizing that I will not, in fact, get caught up with everything if I have “just one more day”. Awesome. 🤙 Tomorrow will be different, tho, I’ll get caught up tomorrow for sure…

America needs a reality show where people are forced to read the things they post online in-person to the people they are attacking. Social media has absolutely broken our brains and how we treat each other.

Worth naming carefully: delay is being framed as administrative lag, but it functions as a removal mechanism without a removal order. When Work authorization expires, E-Verify flags it.

Two more details to track: USCIS has placed renewals from Venezuelan applicants on adjudicative hold under Presidential Proclamations 10949 and 10998. And congressional offices report that expedite requests are being limited to health care workers.

NOTUS documented the pattern this weekend: a firefighter paramedic 6 months into a pending renewal; a child behavioral therapist; a city council staffer; a 25-year-old video game tester who lost his job in January.

The slowdown is measurable. Per the National Immigration Forum, USCIS completed 18% fewer cases in Q2 FY 2025 than in the same quarter the year before. USCIS recommends applying 150–180 days before expiration.
